note: v1 92.69 (seeds 0/11 92.69/92.70), When the Tape Runs Out, the closer: chillwave dusk at 78 bpm. A soft electro-kit (12-bit crushed) and a juno pad that breathes against the kick (sidechain duck) and warbles on wM's tape deck, under a dreamy wordless vox line (dream-vox), a slow arpeggio with a dotted-eighth tape echo, a pulsing analog bass and crackle; Dmaj9 Bm11 Gmaj7#11 A6sus. THE RUN-OUT is the form: after the full band every section loses a voice (kick, then arp, then bass) until the vox and pad are alone, and the tape stops over the last bar. Draft 88.5 -> 92.7: a dotted clave and the arp's 3/16 echo for off-grid motion, low end and loudness for the lo-fi master range.

v2 92.92 (seeds 0/11 92.92/93.19 vs v1 re-scored 92.69/92.70): the closer gets its LAST WORD and a longer middle. Over the bare pad in the end section, as the tape starts to sag, the dream-vox sings its first phrase once more, softer each bar, before the tape stops - the album ends on the melody, not just on the pad. The vox's full B section grows from 16 to 24 bars (the song's high point, before the run-out starts taking voices away), and the dotted-eighth clave now runs from the first groove (A) - rhythm 73 -> 89-91.

v3 95.30 (seeds 0/11 95.30/92.98 vs v2 re-scored 92.92/93.19; pin a9affd66): THE SWEEP. The arpeggio now lives behind chirper-two's new resonant ladder filter (q 9): nearly shut through the first groove, it opens across the whole 24-bar vox section (450 Hz to about 4 kHz) - the sunset's peak - and closes again through the first run-out before the arp leaves, so the closer has one long breath in and out. The whole song also takes wM's fixed feel drift (4 ms wandering over 4-bar spans), so the machine groove loosens like a tired tape.

v4 92.11 kept on judgment (seeds 0/11 92.11/89.99 vs v3 re-scored today 92.84/90.59, about -0.7: compscore's rhythm term reads the chewed bars as off-pulse): THE TAPE CHEWS. In the last two bars of the third run-out - only the vox and the pad left - the deck starts eating the tape: wM's chop fx on the master cuts each bar into eight slices and replays them with doubles, reversals and gaps (0 0 r1 . 3 r3 _ 5) before the end section, where the vox sings its last phrase and the tape stops. The title happens in the music now: the tape audibly runs out before it stops.
